title: Clean a desktop PC safely
description: Remove dust from the inside of a computer and clean its peripherals without causing damage.
objectives: Prepare a computer and the workspace for cleaning.
Remove dust with compressed air the safe way.
Clean the keyboard, mouse and monitor with the right materials.
tools: Compressed air (canned or an electric duster)

safety.text: Unplug the computer and wear a grounded wrist strap before cleaning inside.
Never use a household vacuum inside a computer: it builds up static electricity. Only use an ESD-safe vacuum.
Never spray liquid directly onto equipment. Put it on the cloth first.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: Shut down, unplug, press the power button to drain power, and put on the wrist strap. Take the computer somewhere well ventilated or outdoors, since a lot of dust will come out. Wear a dust mask.

steps.title: Blow out the dust
steps.body:
Open the side panel and use short bursts of compressed air:

- **Hold each fan still** with a finger or a non-metal tool while blowing. A spinning fan can be damaged and can push current back into the board.
- Keep the can **upright**. Tilted, it can spray freezing liquid propellant.
- Work from the top down and blow dust **out** of the case, not deeper in.
- Clear the CPU cooler fins, graphics card, PSU fan grille (from outside) and the dust filters.

steps.title: Clean the dust filters
steps.body: Most cases have removable filters at the front, top or bottom. Take them out, tap or rinse them, and let them dry **completely** before refitting.

steps.title: Clean the peripherals
steps.body:
- **Keyboard:** turn it upside down and tap; blow between the keys; wipe the keys with a cloth lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol.
- **Mouse:** wipe the body and feet; clear the sensor window with a dry cotton bud.
- **Monitor:** wipe gently with a dry microfibre cloth. For marks, use a cloth slightly dampened with water or screen cleaner. Avoid ammonia or strong solvents, which damage screen coatings.

steps.title: Check while you are inside
steps.body:
Cleaning is a good time to spot problems:

- Fans that do not spin freely or are noisy
- Swollen or leaking capacitors on the motherboard
- Loose cables and connectors
- Dust caked onto heatsinks, which causes overheating

Note anything you find for the customer.

steps.title: Close up and schedule
steps.body:
Refit the panel, reconnect and confirm the computer starts. Check temperatures if you can.

A dusty environment (near a road, a workshop, pets) needs cleaning every **3 months**; an office every **6–12 months**.

expectedResults: Fans, heatsinks and filters are free of dust.
The computer starts normally and runs cooler.

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting fans spin freely under compressed air.
commonMistakes.why: Over-spinning can damage the fan bearings and the fan can act as a generator.
commonMistakes.fix: Hold each fan still while you blow it out.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a household vacuum cleaner inside the case.
commonMistakes.why: It generates static electricity that can damage components.
commonMistakes.fix: Use compressed air or an ESD-safe vacuum.

commonMistakes.mistake: Spraying cleaner straight onto a monitor or keyboard.
commonMistakes.why: Liquid runs inside and can short circuits.
commonMistakes.fix: Dampen the cloth, not the device.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why hold the fans still while using compressed air?
knowledgeChecks.answer: Spinning them too fast can damage the bearings, and a spinning fan can generate current back into the board.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you use to clean a monitor?
knowledgeChecks.answer: A dry microfibre cloth, or one slightly dampened with water or screen cleaner. No ammonia or strong solvents.
